Every dollar in your wallet is a death certificate with a president's face on it.

I know that sounds dramatic. It isn't. It's actually underselling it.

On Wishonia, we used rocks as currency for 400 years before someone pointed out that rocks are heavy and also everywhere. We switched to a trust-based ledger system in about 12 minutes. Your species took until 2009 to even consider it, and then you mostly used it to buy drugs and pictures of monkeys.

But your money problem is worse than inconvenience. Your money is a weapon, and it's pointed at you, by the people who print it.

## The Pattern: Print Money, Kill People, Repeat

Here's a historical pattern that definitely won't repeat itself (it will):

### Revolutionary France (1790s)

![France fights war, runs out of money, prints money, money becomes worthless. It's like a tutorial level for economic collapse.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-revolutionary-france-1790s-bw-academic.jpg)

France started wars with everyone. Ran out of money. Invented a solution: print fake currency called "assignats" backed by church land they'd stolen.

Backing money with crime is surprisingly honest about what money is.

Hyperinflation hit 13,000% in five years. Napoleon happened. Not great.

### Weimar Germany (1920s)

Germany lost World War I. Printed money to pay reparations. Achieved 29,500% monthly inflation, which means a loaf of bread that cost one mark in January cost billions by fall.

People burned money for heat because paper was worth more as fuel than as currency.

Hitler happened. Really not great.

### United States (1917-present)

- 1913: Created the Federal Reserve
- 1917: Immediately used it to fund World War I
- 1917-present: Dollar has lost 96% of its value
- Wars: Now continuous and everywhere

You're living it right now, reading this sentence with money that's worth 4 cents on the 1913 dollar. How's that working out?

![Create Federal Reserve in 1913. Federal Reserve prints money for wars. Dollar loses value. Fight more wars. Print more money. The circle continues until someone notices.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-united-states-1917-present-bw-academic.jpg)

The pattern is so consistent it's basically a law of physics: give politicians a money printer, they will use it to kill people. Every time. Without exception. For thousands of years.

You invented money to trade chickens more efficiently. Within a few centuries, you were using it to incinerate cities. Remarkable species.

## 1971: When Nixon Weaponized Money Against You

August 15, 1971. The day your money stopped meaning anything and nobody told you.

![Nixon cuts dollar from gold, freezes wages and prices, taxes imports. All at once. Like performing surgery with a sledgehammer.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-1972-when-nixon-weaponized-money-against-you-bw-academic.jpg)

Nixon went on TV and said, in slightly more presidential language:

- "Remember how dollars could be exchanged for gold? We're stopping that."
- "Also, wage and price controls."
- "Also, import taxes."

He called it a "New Economic Policy." On your planet, when someone names a policy the opposite of what it does, something terrible is about to happen. (See also: "Patriot Act," "Affordable Care Act," "Department of Defense.")

### Why He Really Did It

The Vietnam War was bleeding money faster than Congress could appropriate it. France wanted their gold back, which was inconvenient because America had been spending it. Raising taxes would cause riots.

The solution was elegant in the way that arson is elegant: just print money forever. Nobody will notice.

(Everyone noticed.)

### What Actually Happened

The gold standard died. Dollar backing became "trust us bro," which is not a monetary policy taught in any economics textbook but is the one your country has been running for 54 years.

Inflation went to the moon. Your savings were slowly murdered in their sleep, one percentage point at a time, while the killer wore a suit and called it "monetary policy."

### The Theft That Followed

![Since 1972, productivity went up 246 percent. Wages went up 115 percent. Someone kept the difference. Guess who.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-the-theft-that-followed-bw-academic.jpg)

Since 1972:

- Productivity went up 246%
- Wages went up 115%

The difference between those two numbers is the largest theft in history, and nobody went to prison because the thieves wrote the laws.

Where'd the money go?

- Wall Street (correct)
- War contractors (also correct)
- You (wrong, thanks for playing; please collect your participation trophy on the way out, it's worth less than it was when you walked in)

### Your 93% Pay Cut (Measured in Something You Can't Print)

Here's the same theft, measured in gold, because gold is the one thing humans can't print.

In 1972, a typical American family earned the equivalent of 191 ounces of gold per year [@census-family-income-1972] [@macrotrends-gold-history]. If your family still earned 191 ounces, your household income would be over $1,030,000.

It is not over $1,030,000.

Median household income is $77,500 [@census-income-2023]. At today's gold price, that buys you 14 ounces.

You went from 191 ounces to 14. A 93% pay cut, delivered one "normal" year at a time, while your leaders assured you the economy was "growing."

It was growing. For them.

### Why Nobody Told You

Even the think tanks supposedly on your side report the gap as roughly $10,000 a year [@epi-productivitypay2024]. That's because they measure it using the government's own rigged ruler:

- CPI-adjusted (the index has been redesigned multiple times, each revision coincidentally reducing reported inflation)
- Starting at 1979 instead of 1971 (conveniently skipping the worst part)
- Counting your employer's overpriced health insurance as "pay"

You're not missing $10,000 a year. You're missing $952,000. The distance between those numbers is not a rounding error. It is the entire game.

Gold doesn't negotiate. Gold doesn't "target 2% inflation." Gold just sits there, being worth what it's worth, silently testifying that your paycheck is an evaporating puddle someone labeled "compensation."

Your economists will say gold is a "volatile commodity." Your economists work for the people who redesigned CPI. Gold didn't go up. The dollar went down. Those are not the same sentence, even though they produce the same chart.

### How the Robbery Works (Same Trick, Different Costume)

On Wishonia, we learned this lesson 6,000 years ago. The trick never changes. Only the costume:

- **Egyptian pharaohs:** "The gods chose us. Hand over your grain and build these pyramids."
- **Medieval kings:** "God appointed us. Hand over your harvest and fight these wars."
- **Modern central bankers:** "Here are 47 pages about hedonic adjustments and geometric weighting in consumer price index methodology."

The current version replaced gods with something far more effective: economics so tedious that your eyes glaze over before you finish the sentence explaining how you're being robbed.

You don't need divine right when you have a central bank. You don't need serfs when you have "inflation targets" and "quantitative easing" and "monetary policy accommodation."

A serf who understands the system is dangerous. A serf who finds the system too boring to understand is a taxpayer.

### Why You Never Learned This in School

The average American with a bachelor's degree completes approximately 17,000 hours of formal education. The number of those hours dedicated to explaining how the Federal Reserve creates money and who gets it first:

Zero.

Not "nearly zero." Zero. You will spend more time learning to play the recorder, which is an instrument designed to make parents regret reproduction.

Here's what monetary policy actually determines:

- Whether your brightest minds design vaccines or warheads
- Whether your factories build MRI machines or missiles
- Whether your wealth cures disease or funds it

Every problem you have (poverty, preventable death, unaffordable housing) is a resource allocation failure downstream of monetary policy. It is the single most consequential force shaping human civilization.

And there is no required course, in any state, at any level, that teaches you how it works.

Only 28 states even require a basic economics course to graduate high school, and those courses cover supply and demand curves, not balance sheet expansion. The thing that took 93% of your purchasing power is not on the test. It has never been on any test.

The priesthood that operates the extraction system designs the curriculum. This is the same way it has always worked.

### The Priesthood

How do you build a priesthood? The same way you always have: fund it.

- Banks endow economics chairs at universities
- The Federal Reserve funds economic research
- Economists rotate between academia, the Fed, and Wall Street (this has a name, "the revolving door," and nobody finds it strange)

Say "the system works" and you get tenure, consulting fees, and a seat on the Federal Reserve Board. Say "the system is theft" and you get called "not a serious economist," which is the modern equivalent of "heretic."

### The Fake Nobel Prize

The crowning achievement: in 1968, Sweden's central bank created a prize and stuck Alfred Nobel's name on it. This gave economics the authority of physics, chemistry, and medicine.

Small problem: Alfred Nobel never authorized it.

The Nobel Prize website itself states that "the prize in economic sciences is not a Nobel Prize" [@nobelprize-economics-not-nobel]. Nobel's great-grandnephew, Peter Nobel, called it "a PR coup by economists to improve their reputation" and noted that Alfred "despised people who cared more about profits than society's well-being" [@nobel-family-dissociation-2010].

Let me restate this in case you read it too fast:

The central bank that prints your money invented a fake Nobel Prize to make the people who defend printing your money look like scientists.

It worked. You call them "Nobel laureates" and nod along when they explain, using terminology designed to sedate you, why your 93% pay cut is actually called "a healthy economy."

On Wishonia, we have a word for this. It translates roughly to "decorating the burglar."

## The Dual Mandate: Optimizing for Serfdom

The Federal Reserve has two official goals:

1. "Maximum employment"
2. "Stable prices" (defined as 2% annual inflation)

On Wishonia, we optimize for "are people's lives getting better?" which is apparently too complicated for Earth. Let me show you what your goals actually optimize for.

### "Maximum Employment" (Everyone Is Busy)

"Maximum employment" means everyone has a job. Not everyone has a *good* job. Not everyone has a job that pays enough to live on. Not everyone has time to read about monetary policy.

Just: everyone is occupied.

A medieval serf working sunup to sundown was maximally employed. So is a modern American working two jobs who can't afford an emergency room visit. The metric literally cannot tell the difference between a thriving middle class and a plantation.

That is not a flaw. It is the point.

Busy people don't ask questions. Busy people don't read Federal Reserve balance sheets. Busy people vote for whichever candidate promises to "create jobs," which is a promise to keep them too busy to notice who's keeping them poor.

### "Stable Prices" (We Take 2% Per Year)

"Stable prices" means 2% inflation per year.

The Federal Reserve's stated, public, announced-on-television goal is to take 2% of your purchasing power annually. They named the theft, put it in a press release, and called it "price stability."

- Over 35 years, 2% compounds to a 50% loss
- Over the 54 years since Nixon, it has taken 93%

They are hitting their target. You are the target.

### The "Deflation Is Dangerous" Lie

The justification, taught in every economics class that bothers to exist: deflation (falling prices) is dangerous because "people won't buy things if they know prices will be lower tomorrow."

Think about that for one second.

- You buy a new iPhone every two years knowing the next one will be better and cheaper
- You bought a flat-screen TV knowing the price drops every year
- You buy a laptop knowing it will be worth half as much in eighteen months

The entire technology sector has experienced continuous deflation for decades, and it is the fastest-growing, most innovative sector of your economy.

People buy things they want. They do not sit in empty rooms waiting for prices to fall further.

The "deflation is dangerous" story is told by the people who benefit from inflation, which is the people who get the new money first, which is not you.

### The One Data Point

The only evidence they ever cite is the Great Depression, where falling prices coincided with economic collapse. This is a correlation/causation error so basic it would fail an introductory statistics course.

The Great Depression's deflation was *caused by* bank failures and credit contraction, not the other way around.

Meanwhile, the longest sustained deflation in American history (1870-1896, known as "the Great Deflation") coincided with the most explosive economic growth your country had ever seen [@bis-deflation-historical-2015]:

- Prices fell roughly 2% per year
- Real output grew 2-3% per year
- Real wages rose
- The railroad, telephone, and electric light were built

The Bank for International Settlements (the central bank of central banks) tested this across 140 years and 38 economies and found that the link between deflation and slower growth is "weak" and "derives largely from the Great Depression" [@borio-costs-deflation-2015].

One data point. They built the entire theology of inflation on one data point that they misread.

Your priests are not very good at science, which is perhaps why they needed that fake Nobel Prize.

### What They Could Measure Instead

Here is a question so obvious it feels stupid to ask: are people's lives actually getting better?

That's it. That's the metric.

You could measure:

- **Inflation-adjusted after-tax median income:** Are people actually getting richer, or just getting bigger numbers on smaller paychecks?
- **Median health-adjusted life years:** Are people living longer, healthier lives, or just working longer before dying of treatable diseases?

These metrics exist. Economists know how to calculate them. No central bank on Earth uses them.

Because if the Federal Reserve were judged by whether the median American is actually healthier and wealthier each year, someone would have to explain why the answer has been "no" for most of the last five decades.

It is much easier to target "maximum employment" and "2% inflation" and declare victory while your citizens work more hours for less purchasing power and die of diseases that could have been cured with the money you printed for banks.

## The Cantillon Effect: Why You're Poor and Raytheon Isn't

The Cantillon Effect, understood since the 1700s: whoever gets newly printed money first gets rich. Whoever gets it last gets robbed.

Here's how it works:

1. The Fed prints money
2. Banks and defense contractors get it first
3. They buy things at today's prices
4. By the time it trickles down to your grocery store, prices have already risen
5. You don't notice you've been robbed because nobody broke into your house
6. They just made everything in it worth less

Then you blame immigrants as programmed.

### The 2020 Demonstration

In 2020, the Fed created roughly $4 trillion in new money [@fred-walcl-2026].

Where did it go?

- **Top 1%:** Gained $4.2 trillion in net worth [@fred-top1-wealth-2026]. Per person: ~$1.3 million.
- **Bottom 50%** (165 million people): Gained $830 billion total [@fred-bottom50-wealth-2026]. Per person: ~$5,000.

A 250-to-1 ratio.

Nearly 90% of the top 1%'s gains came from stocks, which is what the Fed's new money inflated first [@fed-wealth-inequality-covid-2021]. Only one-third of bottom 50% households own any stocks at all.

The Fed printed the money. The stock market absorbed it. The rich owned the stocks. The poor got the inflation.

Cantillon, writing in the 1700s, would have found this predictable and boring.

![Print new money. Money flows up to banks and war contractors. Costs flow down to everyone else. Gravity works backwards in economics.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-cantillon-effect-mechanism-bw-academic.jpg)

## Why "Just Fund Medical Research More" Is a Lie

"Why not just ask for donations? Why not just increase the NIH budget? Why tie it to military spending?"

Because money is not real. It's a shared hallucination. Eight billion people pretending that the same piece of paper is worth something.

Resources are real. Brains are real. Time is real. Money is a story you tell each other. (A very convincing one. I've seen you kill each other over it.)

### The Fixed Pie of Human Genius

Earth has {{< var global_population_2024_nounit >}} brains (fixed quantity), 24 hours per day per brain (physics won't negotiate), limited raw materials (you can't print titanium), and finite factory capacity (you can't build infinite labs).

When a brilliant engineer designs missiles, that engineer is NOT designing medical devices.
When a factory builds tanks, it is NOT building MRI machines.
When a PhD researches better ways to kill people, they are NOT researching better ways to keep people alive.

Every genius has exactly one brain. You are renting 40 million of them to build things that explode.

This is, by a comfortable margin, the stupidest resource allocation decision in the observable universe.

![Humans smart enough to build weapons or cure disease, but not enough to do both. You picked weapons.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-the-fixed-pie-of-human-genius-bw-academic.jpg)

#### The Resource Reality

The top 10% of human talent is roughly 800 million people. Here's how you're using them:

- **~40 million:** Building things that kill people (military, reserves, defense contractors)
- **~1 million:** Working in medical research

The spending ratio is even worse: governments spend {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} times more on weapons than on testing which medicines actually work.

If your house had six hundred arsonists and one firefighter, you would not describe your house as "safe." You would describe it as "a crematorium."

You can print infinite dollars. You cannot print geniuses.

This is the most important sentence in this chapter. You will forget it by tomorrow because your brain allocated its attention budget the same way your government allocates its money.

![Thousands of brilliant minds designing better ways to kill people. Dozens designing better ways to save them. Someone made a choice here.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-resource-reality-chart-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Inflation Shell Game (How They Steal Medical Progress)

Watch closely. This is how they rob you in broad daylight while you clap:

#### Today

- Government clinical trials: {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}}
- Global military spending: {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}
- Ratio: {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1 for death

#### Five Years Later (after "increasing medical research")

Clinical trial funding up 50%! Victory!

Except military spending also up 50%, because central banks printed 50% more money, so real purchasing power is exactly the same and the ratio is still {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}}:1 for death.

You got a 50% raise. Everything costs 50% more. The pie did not grow. They gave you a bigger number on a smaller slice and expected you to say thank you.

You did. You always do.

![Budget goes up 50 percent. Inflation goes up 50 percent. Purchasing power stays the same. You're running to stay in place, like a hamster with a printing press.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-inflation-shell-game-comparison-bw-academic.jpg)

### The Proof: 50 Years of Going Nowhere

#### Medical Research as % of GDP

- 1975: 0.08%
- 1985: 0.07%
- 1995: 0.07%
- 2005: 0.06%
- 2015: 0.06%
- 2025: 0.065%

Absolute dollars increased 10x. Share of actual resources: decreased.

You got richer and spent less of it on not dying. Like buying a bigger house and removing the smoke detectors.

![Medical research as a percentage of GDP from 1975 to 2025. You got richer and spent less of it on not dying. Like buying a bigger house and smaller fire extinguishers.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-medical-research-as-of-gdp-bw-academic.jpg)

#### What Actually Grew

- Financial sector: 3% to 8% of GDP
- Military-industrial sector: 3% to 3.4% of GDP (direct spending; broader defense-adjacent industries add more)
- Healthcare spending: 7% to 18% of GDP (but most of that growth is bureaucracy, not cures)

The part that actually keeps you alive, the actual medical research, is a shrinking slice of a growing pie.

You baked a bigger pie and gave the science department a smaller plate. The money printers fund what they value. They value control, not cures. Nobody ever seized power with a stethoscope. (Though, medically speaking, you could.)

### "Just Tax the Billionaires"

"Fine," says the progressive who just read the last three subsections. "The problem is inequality. Tax the billionaires. Fund medical research. Simple."

Your species has been trying this for a century. Here is the loop:

**Step 1.** Progressives raise taxes on the wealthy. Victory.

**Step 2.** The wealthy spend a fraction of those taxes on [lobbyists who return $18 for every $1 invested](../problem/unrepresentative-democracy.qmd). They secure:

- {{< var us_gov_waste_corporate_welfare >}}/year in direct corporate welfare {{< var us_gov_waste_corporate_welfare_cite >}}
- {{< var us_gov_waste_fossil_fuel_subsidies >}} in fossil fuel subsidies {{< var us_gov_waste_fossil_fuel_subsidies_cite >}}
- {{< var us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies >}} in agricultural subsidies (top 10% of farms collect 63% of payments) {{< var us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies_cite >}}

Over $300 billion per year flows back to the people you just taxed, through programs too boring for voters to monitor and too lucrative for lobbyists to ignore.

**Step 3.** The Federal Reserve prints money. Asset prices inflate. Remember the Cantillon Effect? The top 1% gained $1.3 million each. The bottom 50% gained $5,000 each. The billionaires didn't just recover what you taxed. They made more in asset inflation than they lost in taxes, and the inflation bill went to the same working families progressives were trying to help.

**Step 4.** Progressives look at the widening wealth gap and propose: higher taxes on the wealthy.

Return to Step 1. Repeat for 100 years.

The entire planet spends {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} per year testing whether drugs work in humans {{< var global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual_cite >}}. One country spends over $300 billion per year on corporate handouts to people who already have money. The ratio is roughly 68:1 for subsidizing wealth over testing cures.

Every "tax the billionaires" campaign in history has left this ratio untouched, because the same political system that collects the taxes allocates the spending, and that system has a [documented 0% correlation with what voters actually want](../problem/unrepresentative-democracy.qmd).

The progressive strategy fails not because the diagnosis is wrong (the allocation is obscene) but because it prescribes the same treatment that has failed for a century: route more money through a captured system and hope it comes out different this time.

The money goes in as taxes. It comes out as subsidies, asset inflation, and an NIH that spends {{< var nih_clinical_trials_spending_pct >}} on clinical trials. The pipe leaks faster than you can fill it, and the leaks flow upward.

This is why the [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) doesn't route funding through your existing institutions. It builds a [new pipeline](../solution/dih.qmd) that the lobbyists haven't colonized yet.

You don't fix a rigged game by playing harder. You build a different game.

### Why Money Printing Matters: Resources Follow the Printer

![When you spend money on weapons, the smart people go work on weapons. Then you wonder why nobody's curing your diseases. You built a waterslide into a shark tank and asked where all the swimmers went.](/assets/images/central-banks/central-banks-section-why-money-printing-matters-resources-follow-the-printer-bw-academic.jpg)

When the Fed prints $1 trillion for war, defense contractors get it first and immediately buy up the best engineers, scientists, and factories.

An MIT graduate with $200k in student debt chooses between:

- Raytheon at $150k
- NIH postdoc at $55k

The student debt does not care about your feelings, so neither does the graduate. Another brain lost to the death machine. Multiply by forty million. Then wonder why nobody cured your mother's cancer.

Printing more money for medicine does not work because the Fed prints even more for war, maintaining the same deadly ratio. The hamster wheel spins faster. You stay in the same place.

The only solution: change the ratio. Take from war. Give to life. That's what the [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) does.
